why_next: The first PASS of all four frozen decision conditions (C1-C4) on stochastic infrastructure confirms that SQLite DB-backed sessions, cache TTL expiry, real I/O jitter, and mixed JWT algorithms do NOT break orthogonality at delta=0.15 (CI upper 0.135 < 0.15). This advances C-FRESHNESS from MIXED/deterministic to PASS/stochastic at the mock fidelity level. However, the claim ceiling is bounded to localhost SQLite+cache+mixed-JWT mock. The critical unknown is whether real external APIs with production databases, distributed caches/CDN, network latency, and OAuth/OIDC middleware preserve the near-zero correlation structure. This requires materially different infrastructure (real API endpoints, not mock servers) and is the single highest-upside question for C-FRESHNESS product deployment. At delta=0.10 the experiment is underpowered (CI upper 0.135 > 0.10, needs n~865); the practical significance question (do real APIs preserve orthogonality?) takes priority over the statistical power question.

established: Behavioral-structural signal orthogonality confirmed at delta=0.15 on stochastic Flask 3.1.3 + SQLite WAL-mode + in-memory cache TTL=0.5s + jitter 10-100ms + PyJWT HS256/RS256 on localhost: pooled r=0.0463 (r2=0.002), 95% CI [-0.0434, 0.1353], CI upper 0.1353 < 0.15. TOST p_upper=0.011 at delta=0.15. Shared variance < 1.83% at CI upper bound. n=480 paired samples from 8 co-occurring conditions x 60. Audit PASS confirms all metrics recomputed.

Behavioral signals (token validation failure rate, session state change, auth boundary shift, session_status_check) remain a validated detection dimension: TP=1.0 (Wilson lower 0.9398 > 0.75) across 8 co-occurring conditions with stochastic DB/cache/jitter/mixed-JWT. First PASS of all four frozen decision conditions (C1 TP=1.0, C2 8/8 variance, C3 CI upper 0.135, C4 FP=0.0) on stochastic infrastructure.

Stochasticity does not break orthogonality: deterministic baseline r=0.0335 CI upper 0.123 (parent EXP-GRAPH-35330739886) vs stochastic r=0.0463 CI upper 0.135 — shift of +0.0128 in point estimate and +0.012 in CI upper bound, both within sampling variation, both below delta=0.15 threshold. Demonstrates stochastic DB/cache/jitter/mixed-algorithm does not introduce material correlation.

Power analysis: at n=480, minimum detectable |r|=0.0895. Observed |r|=0.0463 below detectable threshold — experiment is equivalence-powered at delta=0.15, not significance-powered for point estimate. Minimum n for |r|=0.05 is 1538. Minimum n for delta=0.10 is ~865.

Six structural signal families remain falsified for C-FRESHNESS frozen gate in deterministic mock: Jaccard, TF-IDF, response-time KS, linear Fisher LDA ensemble, field-usage profiling, direct schema comparison.

recommended_action: Design a graph lane experiment testing behavioral-structural orthogonality on REAL external API endpoints (not mock servers). Candidates: (1) a self-hosted production-like REST API with real PostgreSQL/MySQL DB, Redis/Memcached cache, and OAuth2/OIDC middleware; or (2) a public API with rate limiting, cache headers, and CDN (e.g., GitHub REST API, Stripe test mode). The experiment should measure whether |r| < 0.15 persists when: (a) behavioral signals come from real JWT/OAuth validation, session state, and permission checks against a production database; (b) structural signals come from real schema/documentation endpoints with cache-Control, ETag, and CDN variation; (c) stochastic variation includes DB replication lag, cache eviction, network latency, and production middleware. If orthogonality holds at delta=0.15 on real APIs, C-FRESHNESS can advance toward VALIDATED. If |r| exceeds 0.15, the product must pivot to fused classifiers. Do NOT increase n to 865 for delta=0.10 until real-API orthogonality is established — the practical significance question is more important than statistical power at this stage.
